questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to study in USA

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The reason I am only giving 8 and not 10 was because we were only 7 exchange students at the university, why I really had to work hard to get to know people outside of the university if I wanted more friends

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I would not say very easy, because I received most information very late

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: The person at UC Law SF who was "in charge" of us was very reachable from the beginning, and especially when I arrived

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was easy finding - through Airbnb, Craigslist or Facebook, but it is also expensive and you have to do a bit of work yourself. I travelled there 2 weeks prior to orientation to find housing

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Housing off campus is actually cheaper then on campus. And the campus is in the middle of Tenderloin, which is a very bad neighbourhood due to drugs and crime, so it is not possible to walk around in the night and the neighbourhood is not cozy at all.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was not avaliable for exchange students untill the very end

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was easy enough but most of the classes were already full when we were applying

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: We had to be ready at a certain time and then apply - you could also choose to be waitlisted

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The responsible people at the university was very helpfull

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: in the end - very succesfull

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Just sign up for the waitlist - eventually I got all my waitlisted classes

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Some of them were easy, some were harder. Similar to CPH

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was very similar. Some teachers were demanding activity from the students, some were just talking without including the students - just like in CPH

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Real Estate Transactions, Race, Racism & American Law, Corporate Finance, Contracts

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Contracts was a first year course so it was very basic and the professor was a good teacher. I would recommend this the most.

questions.answer: The university wanted us to buy another American insurance than my Danish one which was around 15.000,00 DKK but luckily I convinced them that I did not need it.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food was very expensive, both goind out and groceries

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The bars close at 2AM

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Not many - I was actually disappointed with this compared to the many ones in UCPH

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Going out, playing tennis, walking around the city, traveling California,

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Lake Tahoe, LA, Las Vegas

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: This was complicated because the American students were not really interested in the exchange students so you would have to do a lot of work yourself.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Americans are very superficial

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Americans are good at giving compliments

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Apply for scholarships early on - I started a year before going 
Go to the city 1-2 weeks before to get to know the city and to find housing
Try to get to know the LLM's or exchange students at other universities

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: You are not many exchange students

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Getting to live in a big american city on your own.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Probably living with people I did not know

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
